item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Freedom House rated Egypt's internet environment 28/100 (Not Free) for the June 2022–May 2023 coverage period and reported severe constraints, including criminal penalties, harassment, surveillance, self-censorship, detention and abuse of online activists, and negligible meaningful political opposition under President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers June 2022–May 2023, overlapping most of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the governing framework and security practices to the Sisi government and Egyptian authorities; it does not establish that Sisi personally directed each reported act.","limitations":["The document is a country-level assessment and does not independently prove personal involvement in every practice."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"During the coverage period, authorities continued blocking news websites; Al-Manassa was blocked for 72 hours after criticizing the lack of mechanisms to hold the president accountable, and more than 150 people were detained and investigated under counterterrorism charges for using social media to mobilize protests around COP27.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The blocking incident occurred in July 2022 and the COP27 detentions in November 2022, within the report's June 2022–May 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The reported actions were taken by Egyptian authorities during Sisi's presidency; the source does not show that Sisi personally ordered them.","limitations":["The exact number of COP27 detainees was not transparent."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":4,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The state retained substantial legal and infrastructural control over telecommunications: Article 67 permits authorities, including national security and military bodies, to commandeer networks in broadly defined national-security circumstances; most telecommunications infrastructure belongs to state-linked Telecom Egypt; and VoIP restrictions were restored after a temporary COP27 lifting.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The legal and ownership arrangements predate 2023; the restoration of VoIP restrictions occurred during the coverage period.","ruler_attribution":"These are state laws, ownership structures, and regulatory practices operating under the Sisi government; personal presidential authorship is not established.","limitations":["Some cited legal and ownership facts are historical context rather than new 2023 actions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The National Telecommunication Regulatory Authority is subordinated to the communications ministry; its board is selected by the prime minister and includes defense, interior, national-security, presidential, and other official representatives. The NTRA previously participated in the 2011 communications shutdown, while in 2022 it fined providers 11.2 million Egyptian pounds and ordered 3.8 million pounds in customer refunds, and separately fined providers 24 million pounds for quality violations.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.9","5B.5","8B.4","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The institutional structure is historical; the fines and refunds occurred in 2022 and inform the 2023-period institutional context.","ruler_attribution":"The regulatory structure and enforcement actions were undertaken by Egyptian state institutions under Sisi's presidency; the source does not attribute the decisions personally to him.","limitations":["The enforcement actions show consumer-protection activity but do not establish regulatory independence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":8,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Egyptian authorities continued using website-blocking powers: 12 websites were blocked in 2022, Al-Manassa was blocked after criticizing presidential accountability, and many news and rights websites remained inaccessible, including sites blocked since 2017; Mada Masr was briefly accessible during COP27 and then re-blocked.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The 2022 actions and continuing blockages fall within the June 2022–May 2023 reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The restrictions are attributed to Egyptian authorities and regulators during Sisi's presidency, not specifically to a personal order by Sisi.","limitations":["The report records the restrictions and stated grounds but does not resolve the chain of command for each blocking decision."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":9,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Authorities and aligned actors pressured publishers and users to remove critical content; at least seven prisoners released before COP27 reported that the National Security Agency ordered them to delete critical social-media content or face arrest, and refusals led to re-arrest. The report also describes state-linked online propaganda and media instructions through intelligence- and interior-ministry WhatsApp groups.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The prisoner-content orders occurred around COP27 in November 2022; the broader media-control practices are historical context reported in the same assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Egyptian security agencies and state-linked media actors under Sisi's government; personal presidential direction is not demonstrated.","limitations":["Some propaganda examples predate 2023 and the source relies partly on reported accounts and studies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":13,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"Egypt's media regime imposed licensing, capital, fee, blocking, content-removal, fines, and imprisonment risks on online outlets and large social-media accounts; independent outlets faced revenue losses from blocking, while online political and social mobilization was restricted and more than 150 COP27-related users were detained or investigated.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","5B.4","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The COP27 detentions and the continuing regulatory environment fall within the reporting period; several laws and licensing rules predate it.","ruler_attribution":"The laws and enforcement environment operated under the Sisi government; the source does not establish that Sisi personally implemented each measure.","limitations":["The regulatory provisions are described as a framework; the source does not quantify enforcement of every provision during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":16,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"Although Egypt's constitution nominally guarantees media freedoms, constitutional amendments adopted in 2019 extended Sisi's possible tenure to 2030 and increased presidential control over the judiciary and the military's political and judicial authority. After the state of emergency formally ended in 2021, many emergency-style restrictions were permanently codified; broad cybercrime and antiterror laws imposed severe penalties for online expression.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.2","4B.4","4B.8","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"These are pre-2023 institutional changes that remained operative during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly identifies Sisi as the president who signed or benefited from the constitutional changes and describes laws enacted under his rule.","limitations":["The facts describe formal legal powers and penalties, not the outcome of every individual case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":18,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"During the coverage period, Mohamed Ali received a life sentence in absentia for online mobilization; Salma El-Shimy received a two-year prison sentence and fine for TikTok content; authorities continued recycling detainees; and Mohamed el-Baqer was released in July 2023 after nearly five years in detention.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The Mohamed Ali sentence and Salma El-Shimy sentence occurred in January and April 2023; el-Baqer's July 2023 release falls just after the report's stated coverage endpoint but within the supplied 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"Cases were processed by Egyptian prosecution and courts under Sisi's government; the source does not establish personal presidential involvement. The release is a favorable institutional outcome but not attributed to Sisi.","limitations":["The source reports allegations and case outcomes without adjudicating the factual basis of the charges."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":20,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"Egyptian law required personal data for SIM activation and .eg domain registration, restricted encryption without approval, and allowed surveillance with limited transparency. The COP27 app reportedly requested extensive personal data and location access and could listen to conversations, read emails, track texts, and bypass encryption; Egyptian authorities denied some allegations.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.5","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The COP27 app issue arose in November 2022; the legal and surveillance framework remained relevant during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The laws and app operated through Egyptian state institutions under Sisi's government; personal presidential authorization is not established. The government's denial is preserved as a qualification.","limitations":["The app's capabilities were reported by cybersecurity experts and disputed by an Egyptian official."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":22,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"Egyptian law allowed state agencies to obtain provider-held user data without judicial orders; providers had to retain data for 180 days and assist surveillance, with large fines and possible license revocation for noncompliance. The 2020 data-protection law exempted national-security authorities, lacked an independent regulator, and remained suspended for lack of executive regulations at the end of the coverage period.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.5","4B.9","5B.7","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The legal provisions predate 2023 but remained in effect or incompletely implemented during the reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The framework was enacted and administered by Egyptian state institutions under Sisi's presidency; the source does not attribute each provision personally to him.","limitations":["The suspended data-protection law represents an implementation failure, but the report does not identify the responsible official."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":24,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"The report documented enforced disappearance, alleged beatings and electric shocks, detention and ill-treatment connected to online activity, state-linked targeting of LGBT+ people using digital evidence, and an anti-LGBT+ online hate campaign during the coverage period.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.7","3B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report presents these as continuing practices, with the anti-LGBT+ campaign explicitly occurring during the coverage period; several individual incidents predate 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Egyptian security forces, prison authorities, and other actors under Sisi's government; personal presidential direction is not established.","limitations":["Some incidents are historical examples used to characterize continuing patterns."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8b599f84f16e49d7","start_unit":25,"end_unit":26,"fact_summary":"During the coverage period, Kaspersky reported that international hacking teams targeted Egyptian government institutions for espionage and data theft; separately, reports described large-scale exposure of Egyptian WhatsApp numbers and malware infections among Egyptian users.","question_ids":["1B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The government-institution cyberattacks were reported in May 2023; other cyber incidents provide contemporaneous context.","ruler_attribution":"The report does not attribute the external attacks to Sisi or establish a specific government response.","limitations":["These facts concern external cyber threats and do not demonstrate ruler performance except by establishing the risk environment."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The document is a Freedom House country report covering June 2022–May 2023, so some historical laws and incidents are contextual rather than events occurring in calendar 2023.","The source generally reports actions by Egyptian authorities or institutions and rarely establishes Abdel Fattah el-Sisi's personal direction, knowledge, or response."]}
